title: What Is Calima in Madeira, and Does It Affect Boat Trips?
description: Calima is a haze of Saharan dust carried to Madeira on east or south winds. It dims the view and reddens the sunset, but wind and waves decide if a trip runs.
heroAlt: Orange sun dimmed by Saharan dust haze over the sea, seen past a boat's bow

images.prompt: From the bow of a white 9 metre motor boat with grey cushioned seats and a dark canopy off Madeira's south coast in the early evening: the sky is a milky, dusty yellow and the sun is a soft orange disc sinking into haze well above the horizon. The sea has a copper sheen. The cliffs of Cabo Girão are a faint grey shape in the haze to one side. No faces, realistic photo, natural colours, no text.
images.alt: Orange sun dimmed by Saharan dust haze over the sea, seen past a boat's bow

images.prompt: Funchal bay on a hazy dust day, seen from the sea at midday: the city and the mountains pale and washed out under a white-yellow sky, the water flat and grey-blue, the far coast fading into haze.
images.alt: Funchal bay under a pale yellow Saharan dust haze, seen from the sea

images.prompt: Close detail of a thin film of fine reddish Saharan dust on the white fibreglass deck and the grey seat cushion of a motor boat, a single finger trace drawn through it, soft daylight.
images.alt: Fine reddish Saharan dust settled on a white boat deck and grey cushion
